newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sons of Gwalia Q3 gold output on budget.
newsitem.headline: Sons of Gwalia Q3 gold output on budget.

text.p: Sons of Gwalia Ltd said on Friday that group gold production in the three months to March 31, its third quarter, was in line with budget forecasts at 128,309 ounces.

Sons of Gwalia also referred to drilling results released earlier by Troy Resources NL, showing significant new intercepts at their Cornishman joint venture near Southern Cross in Western Australia. Sons of Gwalia has 51 pct of the venture.
The intercepts, which ranged from five metres at 3.03 grams per tonne to three metres at 43 grams, had extended the strike length of mineralisation at Cornishman to 1,400 metres.
Sons of Gwalia said it had also increased its gold hedging position to 5.05 million ounces as at April 16, from 3.1 million ounces at December 31, 1996.

The hedge book's prices and size meant that Sons of Gwalia's current cash margins on the cost of production would be protected for many years at current production levels of about 500,000 ounces per annum, the company said.

"The size and delivery prices of these contracts will underwrite substantial cash margins for the Company's future gold production which will, in turn, underwrite the Company's increased and aggressive exploration programmes in its three regional belts in Western Australia and in the Tanami region of the Northern Territory," Sons of Gwalia Managing Director Peter Lalor said in a statement.

"The continuing encouraging results from exploration at the Cornishman project at Southern Cross indicates the great potential of the Company's substantial ground position in the major archaean greenstone belts of Western Australia," he said.
Sons of Gwalia's share price was down two cents at A$5.90 at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
